newsitem.title: UK: Two million Britons to shop for power next April.
newsitem.headline: Two million Britons to shop for power next April.

text.p: Ten percent of power consumers, or about two million people nationally, will be able to shop around for their electricity on April 1, 1998, UK electricity regulator Stephen Littlechild said on Monday.

Littlechild, who is overseeing the opening of the electricity supply market, said the eligibility of customers for the first phase of competition would be determined on the basis of specified postal codes.
The second phase, towards the end of May, would cover a further 15 percent of customers in each supply area, some 3.5 million customers nationally.

The third phase, covering 25 percent of customers -- or about six million customers nationally, would be towards the end of July, and the final phase in mid-September would cover the remaining 50 percent of the market, Littlechild added.
He said that in 1998, all 23 million domestic, industrial and commercial customers would be able to switch and choose electricity supplier for the first time.

"It will be a tremendous logistical challenge to ensure that the industry's systems can cope successfully with these changes. Arrangements are being put in place to ensure that the systems are properly trialled and tested before the market opens."
Each of the 14 public electricity suppliers is responsible for introducing new systems to register suppliers in their area and to send data between parties.

Littlechild said he wanted to ensure that customers have access as soon as posible to the benefits of competition in the power supply market -- while ensuring that services to customers are not disrupted by the changes being introduced.
